title: Power Display Icon Dissapearing on restart
author: ckks1411

judgment.rationale: The issue includes a report archive, and a current 0.100.2 user gives a useful boundary: PowerDisplay is enabled and PowerToys is running, but the tray icon is missing after restart until PowerDisplay settings are opened. This is enough to investigate startup/tray initialization.
evidence: The original 0.99.1 report includes a diagnostic ZIP.
Multiple users report PowerDisplay unavailable despite expected startup.
A 0.100.2 user says opening PowerDisplay settings immediately makes the taskbar icon appear and function.
The symptom is associated with restart/startup.
judgment.recommended_action: Queue a focused PowerDisplay startup and tray-icon initialization investigation.

fix_assessment.rationale: The current reproduction boundary is strong, but lightweight evidence does not establish whether module startup, tray registration, or settings activation is the root cause.

proposed_fixes.title: Initialize PowerDisplay and its tray icon during startup
proposed_fixes.root_cause: PowerDisplay is enabled but its startup path does not always create or register the tray icon; opening the settings page triggers initialization that makes the icon appear.
plan: Compare PowerDisplay startup initialization with settings-page activation and identify the missing startup call or ordering dependency.
Make tray-icon creation idempotent and run it after the required PowerToys host state is ready.
Add startup/restart coverage that does not open Settings.
verification: Restart Windows with PowerDisplay enabled and confirm the tray icon appears without opening Settings.
Open Settings afterward and confirm no duplicate icon or initialization occurs.

confidence.rationale: The settings-page trigger is a strong lifecycle boundary, but the exact skipped initialization step is not public.

issue_context.summary: PowerDisplay's tray icon can be absent after restart even while PowerToys is running, then appears when its settings page is opened.
known_information: Opening PowerDisplay settings restores the icon.
The original report archive is available.
inferences: Settings-page activation may trigger initialization that startup missed.
issue_context.analysis: The settings-page boundary makes this a concrete startup lifecycle investigation rather than a general missing-icon report.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the current public issue body, labels, assignees, and up to the latest 20 public comments returned by GitHub.
Kept the existing dashboard read-only; no dashboard files were modified or published.

actions.label: Approve initialize powerdisplay and its tray icon during startup
actions.note: Approve/start the fork-side design workflow from this public-evidence fix plan. No upstream write occurs from this action.

actions.label: Reproduce Power Display Icon Dissapearing on restart
actions.note: Maintainer-side reproduction reduces the recorded implementation uncertainty without asking the reporter to perform code investigation.

prerequisites: PowerDisplay enabled and its icon configured to appear in the notification area.
steps: Wait for PowerToys startup without opening Settings.
Open the PowerDisplay settings page and check again.
reproduce.expected_result: The icon is present after startup and opening Settings does not change module initialization.
reproduce.observed_result: The icon is absent until the PowerDisplay settings page is opened.
